title: Pastry Chef Salary: Award Rates, Casual Loading, and Annual Conversion
description: Find the pastry chef salary under the Hospitality Award. See minimum hourly rates, casual loading, super, and how to convert to annual pay using 38 hours per week.
salarySummary: A qualified pastry chef under the Hospitality Industry (General) Award 2020 earns at least $29.45 per hour (Level 4), equating to $58,193 per year for a full-time 38-hour week before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a pastry chef under the Hospitality Award?
faqs.a: Under the Hospitality Industry (General) Award 2020, a pastry chef is classified as a Cook (tradesperson). The minimum hourly rate for a Level 4 Cook (tradesperson grade 3) is $29.45 per hour as of 1 July 2026. More experienced pastry chefs at Level 5 or 6 earn $31.30 or $32.13 per hour respectively. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission and are higher than the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to a pastry chef's pay?
faqs.a: Casual employees under the Hospitality Award receive a 25% loading on top of the ordinary hourly rate. For a Level 4 pastry chef, the casual rate is $29.45 × 1.25 = $36.81 per hour. This loading compensates for entitlements like paid leave. Superannuation is paid on top of the casual rate, as the loading is considered part of ordinary time earnings for super guarantee purposes.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: To estimate your annual gross salary, multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours per week and then by 52 weeks. For a full-time pastry chef working 38 hours per week at $29.45 per hour: $29.45 × 38 × 52 = $58,193.20. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a fortnightly figure, multiply the weekly amount by 2. Remember that super (12%) is paid on top of this gross amount, and tax is deducted based on ATO rates.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Pastry Chef Salary Under the Hospitality Award

If you are looking for a **pastry chef salary** in Australia, the starting point is the Hospitality Industry (General) Award 2020 (MA000009). This award covers cooks, kitchen attendants, and food and beverage staff. The Fair Work Commission publishes minimum rates in the Modern Awards Pay Database, and the latest update from 1 July 2026 sets clear pay levels.

A qualified pastry chef is typically classified as a Cook (tradesperson). Under the award, the minimum hourly rates are:

- Level 4 (Cook grade 3): $29.45 per hour
- Level 5 (Cook grade 4): $31.30 per hour
- Level 6 (Cook grade 5): $32.13 per hour

These rates apply to full-time and part-time employees. For a full-time pastry chef working 38 ordinary hours per week, the weekly minimum is $1,119.10 (Level 4). That works out to an annual gross salary of $29.45 × 38 × 52 = **$58,193.20**.

### How the National Minimum Wage Compares

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. A pastry chef under the award earns more than this minimum because the award recognises trade qualifications. So when you research a **pastry chef salary**, always check the relevant award classification rather than the national minimum.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

Many pastry chefs work casually. The award requires a 25% casual loading on top of the ordinary hourly rate. For a Level 4 pastry chef:

- Ordinary rate: $29.45 per hour
- Casual rate: $29.45 × 1.25 = $36.81 per hour
- Annual casual equivalent: $36.81 × 38 × 52 = $72,736.56

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary time earnings. For casual employees, the casual loading is part of ordinary time earnings, so super is calculated on the casual rate. However, super stops once your earnings reach the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27).

### Fortnightly Pay

If you are paid fortnightly, multiply your weekly pay by two. For a full-time Level 4 pastry chef:

- Weekly: $1,119.10
- Fortnightly: $2,238.20

This helps when budgeting or comparing salary offers.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

To estimate your take-home pay, use the 2026–27 Australian resident tax rates:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners).

For a full-time pastry chef earning $58,193:

- Tax: approximately $7,978
- Medicare levy: approximately $1,164
- Net annual take-home: around $49,051

This is an estimate. It does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

## Using the Timesheet and Pay Guides

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, along with estimated tax and super. Remember: never enter a rate that already includes casual loading – use the checkbox to add it.

For official pay rates, always refer to the [pay guides](/blog) published by the Fair Work Ombudsman. They contain the minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates for each award. The Fair Work Commission also provides the Modern Awards Pay Database with downloadable spreadsheets.

### What About Average Weekly Earnings?

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full-time adults at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). That is higher than the award pastry chef salary because it includes higher-paid roles. For all employees (including part-time), the average is $1,579.20 per week. These figures help you see where the award rate sits in the broader market.

## Key Takeaways

- A **pastry chef salary** under the Hospitality Award starts at $29.45 per hour (Level 4).
- Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks.
- Casual employees get 25% loading, and super is 12% on top.
- Use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to compare offers.
- Always check the award classification for your skill level.

For more detail on casual pay, see our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page. And remember that the award prevails over any data extract – if in doubt, consult the Fair Work Ombudsman.
